Salut, c'est Lela!C’est avec une grande: Hi, it’s Lela! It is with great pride and immense pleasure that I introduce the fall 2022 cohort of École Converse! Since its beginnings, La Converse has gradually transformed to become a school as well. We often work with people who have little or no training in journalism, and we turn them into journalists.
Cette approche nous permet de démocratis: This approach allows us to democratize the profession and to build, from within, a media outlet that looks like us – one that represents our neighbourhoods and our realities. École Converse began as a pilot project with two editions: the first was held online in 2021 with the Université du Québec en Outaouais (UQO) and trained 25 students in dialogue journalism; the second was held in person last spring and gave us the chance to welcome and train 4 apprentice journalists: Fatima Bah, Ahmed El Moudden, Naila Naoui and Marc-Elder Piard. Now, École Converse is an integral part of La Converse. This summer, Marc and Fatima even continued their journey with us and were selected for the scholarships that La Converse awards for dialogue journalism.
Au cours d’une soirée informelle à nos b: During an informal evening at our offices, our students told us they wanted to continue École Converse in the fall. Ahmed is therefore back for a second year, and Fatima is continuing her learning through her scholarship and joining the fall cohort to hone her skills. They are joined by Melissa, Djazia, Youveline and Hadiatou. Without further ado, let me introduce them to you through portraits they wrote about one another.
‍<strong>P.-S. : Vous aimez notre travai: ‍P.S.: Do you like our work and want to see us do more, all while keeping the young people we train? Subscribe to La Converse and make a contribution that will help us carry out our mission: to represent and serve marginalized communities through dialogue journalism, to build bridges and to be a space for social change.
Ahmed, de son nom complet Ahmed El Moudd: Ahmed, whose full name is Ahmed El Moudden, is a young Quebecer from a culturally diverse background. He knows Morocco through the eyes of his parents, who instilled in him open-mindedness and curiosity. One of his best childhood memories is the moment he received a computer – that gift planted in him a love of multimedia. Design, programming and creation: his creative side is expressed today in his involvement in his community and in his ideas. Our series “Hood Heroes” is the result of one of the ideas he shared with us during École Converse last spring. At La Converse, Ahmed has found his place. He manages to express himself through his graphic design and draws inspiration from young people so that he, in turn, can give back and inspire. Mindful of the future and eager to push himself, Ahmed takes the time needed to succeed at everything he undertakes and is always looking for new challenges.
Personne optimiste et intelligente, Djaz: An optimistic and intelligent person, Djazia also combines eloquence, analytical skill and curiosity. A recent political science graduate, she wants to understand the world around her and promote inclusive, unifying values. That is why she decided to go into journalism. Through École Converse, this young woman hopes to learn how to present everyone’s experiences and history with sensitivity. Having emigrated from Algeria at the age of 13, she says she witnessed the dangers and negative consequences of the misrepresentation of marginalized communities. These communities include immigrants, racialized people and Muslims. After working hard on the way she sees the world, Djazia is now a positive force ready to put herself at the service of others.
Curieuse et passionnée : ces deux mots d: Curious and passionate: these two words describe Fatima perfectly. At 18, this Montréaler is in her second edition of École Converse. A lover of history and journalism, she has found at La Converse an environment that is conducive to learning and gives a voice to all communities: she believes it is important to equip them through her reporting. She also told us she fell in love with the team!
« Pour moi, tout est politique ; et c’es: “For me, everything is political; and it’s important to understand politics to understand how our lives work.” That is the sentence the interview with Melissa, a young political science student, begins with. Melissa defines herself first and foremost as a Montréaler, because Montréal is the city where she was born and raised. Very sociable, she exudes confidence and is always the first to approach others to get to know them. When asked what drove her to sign up for École Converse, the young woman answers that, given the way she sees things, it was a no-brainer. Indeed, Melissa is determined to give a voice to communities and to present the different points of view on any subject. For the student, La Converse was the perfect place for that.
Youveline est une jeune femme à l’aube d: Youveline is a young woman on the cusp of her twenties with an immense desire to understand and connect with others. She was born in Haiti but spent most of her childhood in the Turks and Caicos Islands, where she was immersed in a community-oriented culture. Next November, she will celebrate her 10th anniversary in Montréal, but it hasn’t always been easy for Youveline in the metropolis. As a Black immigrant woman who didn’t speak French, she had to face various systemic and social obstacles. It was through community and civic engagement that she found herself and found her purpose. These experiences will guide her work at La Converse, particularly in decoding social issues with a sensitive and caring approach. She believes that small changes can have a ripple effect and lead us toward a more just, and therefore happier, world. She is joining La Converse in the hope that this platform will amplify ignored voices in the name of progress and allow her to develop the skills needed to keep serving others and her community.
Originaire de Guinée, Hadiatou Diallo, a: Originally from Guinea, Hadiatou Diallo, a.k.a. “Hadi,” arrived in Canada at a very young age. She likes interacting with people, reads books on human psychology and studies the humanities. She also likes writing poetry and would like to publish a book one day. She is still working on defining her identity. Indeed, she doesn’t really consider herself a Quebecer, but rather a Canadian. She identifies more with Canadian values and inclusiveness. She joined La Converse to learn more about writing. She also finds that La Converse is more human and more neutral in its articles than some traditional media outlets.
